usageNotes: Commits the assignment plan produced by `get_subscriptions_auto_assign` — always call that endpoint first and pass its full response as `proposal`. The handler validates two digests (pool-config and live node-status) embedded in the proposal and rejects with HTTP 409 if either has changed since the plan was computed, so callers must re-fetch the proposal and retry after any topology or key-pool change. The caller must hold `PRIV_RESOURCE_MODIFY` on each remote referenced in the proposal in addition to the top-level `System.Modify` privilege; an audit-only caller cannot commit a plan even if they rendered the preview.

examples.summary: Commit an auto-assign plan to distribute three subscription keys across two remotes

tips: Always use Content-Type: application/json — the nested proposal object cannot be encoded as form-urlencoded.
A 409 response means the pool or node topology changed between plan generation and commit; re-call get_subscriptions_auto_assign and resubmit.
The returned array lists only the assignments actually persisted — compare against your proposal to detect any partial application.
API tokens are supported (allowtoken: true); scope the token to System.Modify plus per-remote PRIV_RESOURCE_MODIFY.
